comparator.name: Rechtsgeleerdheid
comparator.sourceNotes: The normalized target is the broad Bachelor Rechtsgeleerdheid, whose current official information gives a common 60-EC first year followed by six named graduation tracks. Nederlands Recht is selected under the neutral least-specialized/general route rule because it continues all principal fields of Dutch law and the official page presents it as the broad legal foundation aligned with the requirements for Dutch legal practice. The current official programme page provides a complete 180-EC route: 60 EC in each year. Its single 5-EC third-year restricted choice between introductory legal philosophy and legal sociology is retained as choice space rather than populated to suit UCR.
components: The programme page states that students write their own legal publication in this continuation of the bachelor research line.
Restricted choice: one of the two approved introductory courses.
Practice-based capstone in which students prepare and conduct a case as judge, lawyer or public prosecutor.

routeSelection.basis: The target offers six post-propaedeutic tracks after a common first year. Nederlands Recht is the least specialized route: it continues private, criminal, constitutional and administrative law and adds European and public international law, legal philosophy or sociology, and an integrated student courtroom. This selection follows the target structure and official presentation rather than UCR fit.

selection.assessment: The closest broad law/politics/society programme and the international/European and technology-law directions are all evidenced, feasible and materially distinct. Every pair differs by at least twelve courses (90 EC), so production stops at the three-alternative maximum; the remaining named tax, notarial and legal-public-administration directions are recorded without manufacturing extra curricula.

alternatives.label: Dutch law, politics & society
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines UCR’s full law sequence with politics, sociology, economics, history, research and communication, reflecting the broad Nederlands Recht route without claiming Dutch professional qualification.
alternatives.concept: The closest feasible UCR response to Groningen’s broad Nederlands Recht route: legal foundations and the available private, criminal, constitutional, European and international law courses are integrated with politics, society, economics, history, research and persuasive communication.
progression: Law, Society & Justice in semester 1 precedes every advanced law course that formally requires it. Research Methods & Statistics precedes the selected economics courses with that prerequisite. Introductory politics, sociology, economics and ethics precede advanced EU politics, social theory, public economics, conflict study and research. Every course is offered in its assigned term and every formal prerequisite is completed in an earlier semester.

alternatives.label: Public, international & European law
alternatives.labelReason: The schedule concentrates on international and European law, comparative politics, governance, human rights, conflict and historical context.
alternatives.concept: A distinct international and public-law direction built around public international law, EU law, comparative constitutionalism, governance, human rights, international relations and conflict.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, this route removes criminal and private law, political philosophy, ethics, persuasive communication and negotiation. It adds business foundations, modern and imperial history, the history of warfare, international business governance and social-movement study. Six of the 24 courses differ, and the organising emphasis shifts to public institutions, cross-border orders and their historical and social contexts.
progression: Law, Society & Justice precedes constitutional, international and EU law. Comparative politics, international-relations theory, sociology, economics and research methods precede advanced EU politics, conflict, social theory, international governance and historical research. Business Foundations precedes International Business & Governance. Every course is offered in its assigned term and every formal prerequisite is completed in an earlier semester.

alternatives.label: Technology law, AI & digital regulation
alternatives.concept: A distinct response to the target’s IT-law direction, combining the UCR law sequence with computing, data, AI ethics, business governance and digital transformation.
alternatives.labelReason: The schedule joins law and governance to programming, computing, databases, data science, machine learning, AI ethics, business and digital transformation.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, this route replaces eleven history, politics, sociology, sustainability and communication courses with programming, data science, networks, databases, machine learning, AI ethics, digital strategy, business-and-AI analysis and applied market research. The two programmes share 13 courses and differ by 11 courses (82.5 EC) each way, comfortably clearing the 30-EC floor.
progression: Law, Society & Justice precedes all advanced law courses. Programming precedes networks, Business Foundations precedes Transnational Business Law and digital strategy, and introductory data study precedes machine learning. All formal prerequisites occur earlier, all courses are offered in their assigned Fall 2026 cohort term, and six 300-level courses are included.

notes.text: Groningen provides a cumulative Dutch-law degree across private, criminal, constitutional and administrative law, with Dutch legal research skills, civil and administrative procedure, a student courtroom and the doctrinal coverage required for Dutch legal practice. UCR offers a compact sequence in law, justice, human rights, criminal justice, private law, public international law, comparative constitutional law and EU law, plus related politics and research. The UCR alternatives are academically coherent liberal-arts programmes, but do not reproduce the full Dutch doctrinal and professional sequence or confer civiel effect.
